newsitem.title: MALDIVES: Maldives to resume oil exploration - Trade Ministry.
newsitem.headline: Maldives to resume oil exploration - Trade Ministry.

text.p: The Maldivian government plans to ask international oil companies to resume searching for oil by the end of 1997, a Trade Ministry official said on Wednesday.

"We're processing international tender notices, bidding documents, charts and brochures in an effort to renew interest in prospecting for oil in Maldivian seas," said Ahmed Naseem, the Trade Ministry's Director-General of Foreign Investments.
The government had charted specific areas around some of the atolls of this Indian Ocean archipelago and demarcated a number of plots to explore for oil, Naseem told Reuters.
A preliminary search for oil in the archipelago of 1,192 coral islands was done by a unit of Royal Dutch/Shell Group in the late 1980s, he said.
The company identified three areas for further exploration and bored the seabed in one location in Ari Atoll in 1991 but discontinued their surveys in 1992, he said.
"The company has not discounted the possibility of success, although the incidence of oil has not been recorded so far," Naseem said.

"We're optimistic about parts not covered by the aero-magnetic and seismological surveys and hope to interest international companies in carrying out more extensive exploration to cover the whole country," he added.
The Royal Dutch/Shell unit carried out extensive aerial and marine surveys under an agreement with the government in 1989, he said.
The British Commonwealth Fund will help the Maldives to prepare a plan for the latest oil search, Naseem said.
"Prospectors for oil in the country would be required to sumbit detailed schedules outlining measures to protect the environment," he said.
Given the unique geographical nature of the country, the Maldivian government has formulated extensive controls and policies to protect the environment.
The tourism and fishing, the most dynamic sectors of the tiny nation's economy, depend on sustaining the environment.
